articles.summary: $170M. 15 years. One advanced training center. Elbit Systems will build and operate a simulation hub for the IDF Artillery Corps, supporting the new ROEM and LAHAV systems with AI-enabled training that shortens qualification time and reduces platform wear.
articles.title: Elbit Systems Awarded Approximately $170 Million Contract to Establish and Operate an Advanced Training and Simulation Center for the IDF Artillery Corps

articles.summary: At Elbit Systems' Innovation Week, the company's CTO explored how low-cost threats are challenging traditional defense strategies and why AI and autonomous systems could fundamentally change the way wars are fought.
articles.title: When Cheap Drones Break the Math of War

articles.summary: After Israel Aerospace Industries sold an autonomous submarine to Germany, Elbit is also charging into the undersea world with the acquisition of a Canadian company. “Ukraine’s war against the Russian navy has changed the scene”, says Saar Koursh, head of Elbit’s naval systems sector. Are these the tools that will win the campaign in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb?
articles.title: Submarine warfare: The deal bringing Elbit into the undersea world — and into a battle with Israel Aerospace Industries
Elbit Systems Continues to Expand its Multi-Layered Naval Protection Capabilities to Counter Unmanned and Underwater Threats
